candidate.title: Safe-SeqS
candidate.scope: Safe-SeqS, specifically the assigned middle poster row in which randomly sheared DNA ends serve as UMIs. Its linear route comprises shearing, adapter ligation, the combined amplification/solid-phase-capture block, sequencing, and sequence comparison to infer a rare mutant and its abundance. The matching catalogue page calls this an overview of Safe-SeqS and gives Safe-Seq as an alias. OS-Seq above and the partially clipped Duplex-Seq row below are independently labeled neighboring poster entries with their own arrows, not alternative branches of this assigned schematic. Exogenous PCR-added barcode adaptations and the NOIR and SiMSen-Seq assays discussed in references do not add target workflows. This is a schematic-level implementation within the Safe-Sequencing System family, not a claim that every family implementation uses sheared-end identifiers.

operations.label: Shear
operations.description: Break the input DNA at variable positions. The output is a population of shorter fragments whose randomly generated ends are explicitly labeled as the UMIs.
operations.mechanism: DNA fragmentation by shearing; the particular shearing technology is not given.
operations.information_effect: Creates fragment-end identity while retaining the sequence of the represented DNA segment and any mutation within it. No external barcode assignment is depicted at this step.

operations.label: Align sequences and determine actual ratio
operations.description: Compare the sequence observations and estimate the rare variant and its abundance, represented by the final True mutant glyph. At the Safe-SeqS family level, the primary abstract interprets this comparison through mutation consistency among daughter reads sharing a UID.
